record.paper_title: Developments and open problems on chiral polytopes
record.original_question: Let nr(g) be the number of regular polytopes on orientable surfaces of genus at most g and let nch(g) be the number of chiral polytopes on such surfaces. Determine the limit of nr(g)/nch(g) as g → ∞, if this limit exists.

evidence.quote: Problem 20 Let nr(g) and nch(g) denote respectively the number of regular and chiral polytopes on orientable surfaces of genus at most g. Determine limg→∞ nr(g)/nch(g) if the limit exists.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An abstract polytope of rank $n\ge 3$ is a partially ordered set with elements (faces) ranked from $-1$ to $n$ that satisfies the standard diamond and connectedness conditions modeling a convex polytope combinatorially. The automorphism group $\Gamma(\mathcal P)$ acts freely on the set of flags (maximal chains). A polytope $\mathcal P$ is called regular if $\Gamma(\mathcal P)$ is transitive on flags, and it is called chiral if $\Gamma(\mathcal P)$ has exactly two orbits on flags, with adjacent flags lying in different orbits (so $\mathcal P$ admits all combinatorial rotational symmetries but no reflection).

A rank-3 abstract polytope is equivalent to a map on a surface. For an integer $g\ge 0$, let
$$n_r(g)=\#\{\text{regular polytopes whose underlying surface is orientable of genus }\le g\},$$
$$n_{\mathrm{ch}}(g)=\#\{\text{chiral polytopes whose underlying surface is orientable of genus }\le g\},$$
where polytopes are counted up to isomorphism.

Determine whether the limit
$$\lim_{g\to\infty}\frac{n_r(g)}{n_{\mathrm{ch}}(g)}$$
exists, and if so compute its value.
artifact.category_tag: chiral and regular polytopes on surfaces
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears in a published list of open problems on chiral polytopes and asks for the asymptotic ratio of regular to chiral polytopes counted by orientable genus. While partial enumerations (e.g., complete lists of reflexible and chiral regular maps up to genus 15, and orientable regular maps to genus 101) exist, no published result determines or even establishes existence of this limit. Related work on reflexible-to-chiral ratios addresses different parameters (such as maps with fixed number of faces or fixed type), not the cumulative count by genus.

status_evidence.title: Developments and open problems on chiral polytopes
status_evidence.snippet: Lists open problems including asymptotic comparisons of regular and chiral polytopes on surfaces.
status_evidence.claim: The question is stated as an open problem in a published problem list.

status_evidence.title: Determination of all Regular Maps of Small Genus
status_evidence.snippet: Complete enumeration of reflexible orientable regular maps of genus 2 to 15 and chiral maps of genus 2 to 15.
status_evidence.claim: Only finite-genus enumerations are available; no asymptotic ratio is established.

status_evidence.title: Chiral covers of regular maps of given type
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work on producing chiral maps from regular ones.
status_evidence.claim: Recent constructions do not resolve the asymptotic counting problem.
